questions.prompt: You open under the gun, a tight player 3-bets, you have TT at 100bb. A sound line is…

choices.text: Call or fold to further pressure. Do not 5-bet jam as a default.
Fold to the first open you already made

questions.explanation: Tens are often ahead of a 3-bet and behind a 4-bet or jam. They are not an automatic all-in.

questions.prompt: Button 3-bets your cutoff open, you 4-bet KK, and the button jams 100bb. Against an unknown, the default is…

choices.text: Call. Kings are ahead of a button jam that includes AK and queens.
Fold every time because jams are exactly AA.
Calling a jam is illegal after you 4-bet

questions.explanation: A button jam is wider than a tight UTG jam. Kings are a continue; folding them only because aces exist is a leak.

questions.prompt: Effective stacks are 18bb and you are reraised all-in after your open. Which idea is right?

choices.text: Play exactly as you would at 100bb.
Suited connectors go up in value because stacks are short.
You are priced into more continues, and speculative hands that needed deep implied odds go down.
You must fold AA because the stack is small.

questions.explanation: Short stacks remove room to fold later. Continue with hands that are ahead now, not hands that needed a deep flop.

questions.prompt: You are facing an all-in and the pot already lays you 2 to 1. A hand that wins more than one-third of the time…

choices.text: Cannot be called because it is not a favorite
Must be AA or it loses money
Is a call even when it is not a favorite

questions.explanation: Pot odds, not pride, decide a priced-in call. You do not need to be ahead of 50% when you are getting 2 to 1.
